question: The 5α reductase inhibitor that has been found to be effective both in benign prostatic hypertrophy and male pattern baldness is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "5α reductase inhibitor" -> "reduces dihydrotestosterone levels" -> "improves symptoms of benign prostatic hypertrophy" -> "effective for male pattern baldness" -> "Finasteride" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Finasteride" -> "inhibits 5α reductase" -> "decreases DHT production" -> "beneficial for BPH" -> "also used for hair loss" -> 90%
CHAIN: "5α reductase inhibitor" -> "used in BPH treatment" -> "also effective in male pattern baldness" -> "Finasteride is the only one that fits both" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Flutamide" -> "not a 5α reductase inhibitor" -> "used for prostate cancer" -> "not effective for BPH or hair loss" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Prazosin" -> "alpha-1 blocker" -> "used for hypertension and BPH" -> "not a 5α reductase inhibitor" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Minoxidil" -> "not a 5α reductase inhibitor" -> "used for hair loss" -> "not effective for BPH" -> 70%
analysis: Finasteride is a 5α reductase inhibitor that is effective in treating both benign prostatic hypertrophy (BPH) and male pattern baldness (androgenetic alopecia). Flutamide is an anti-androgen, prazosin is an alpha-1 blocker used for hypertension and BPH, and minoxidil is a vasodilator used for hypertension and as a topical treatment for hair loss but is not a 5α reductase inhibitor.
